html:
Guarani is the language of the Guarani people, spoken today by most Paraguayans. The constitution of 1992 made it an official language of Paraguay alongside Spanish.

Spanish settlers in Asunción took Guarani wives, and their mixed children grew up speaking their mothers' tongue. The Jesuit missions wrote the language down and printed books in it, and in 1639 the Jesuit Antonio Ruiz de Montoya published a great dictionary. Through the War of the Triple Alliance and the Chaco War it was the language of the soldiers.

For a long time Guarani was looked down on in schools and offices, but it never died. Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where most of the population speaks an Indigenous language, and most people switch between the two every day.
sum: Guarani is the language of the Guarani people, spoken today by most Paraguayans. The constitution of 1992 made it an official language of Paraguay alongside Spanish.
